title: Billing / Egress / KMS Acceptance and Legal Triage
summary: Intro call to align procurement/legal checklist and technical acceptance for onboarding Redwood's inference platform. Discussed MSA/DPA redlines, KMS options (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed), egress billing scenarios, SLA thresholds, and a short pilot for performance validation. Action items include sending redline markup, pricing spreadsheet, security package, and scheduling a benchmark run with sample traffic next week.
next_steps: Redwood: Share annotated MSA & DPA draft by 2025-01-15
Redwood: Send pricing & egress scenarios spreadsheet by 2025-01-14
Customer: Review and flag MSA exceptions by 2025-01-20
Schedule SE-led benchmark session week of 2025-01-20 (30-45m)
Legal follow-up meeting 2025-01-22 if redlines require negotiation
action_items: Lina Park: Upload pricing + egress worksheet to shared drive by 2025-01-14
Daniel Ruiz: Prepare benchmark test plan and sample load script by 2025-01-17
Maya Chen: Collate security pack (SOC2 summary, ISO certs, audit contact) and send by 2025-01-15
Laila Gomez: Provide list of required contract concessions by 2025-01-20
transcript:
Header: 2025-01-12 14:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees listed above

[00:00] Lina Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have a lot to cover so we wanna start with the legal and procurement items then move into the technical takeaways — sound okay?
[00:18] Priya Nair: yeah that's good, we've got procurement and legal on deck so we'll try and keep it focused, for context we're trying to get a pilot running in feb so timeline is tight.
[00:32] Sofia Ruiz: hi all, from procurement side our main asks are: clear pricing with egress scenarios, any offramps on data residency, and the MSA/DPA redlines.
[00:45] Lina Park: absolutely, we'll go item by item. quick intro: i'm Lina, i'll be your AE; daniel and maya from SE team will cover the KMS and benchmark stuff. jordan from CS will be a touchpoint during onboarding.
[01:05] Daniel Ruiz: hey everyone, quick technical note — we support hosted, dedicated and private deployments. for pilot usually we do hosted with VPC peering or private link depending on data controls.
[01:18] Omar Haddad: regarding KMS we are pushing to have customer-managed keys, ideally HSM-backed; can you confirm Redwood supports BYOK and our KMS provider?
[01:33] Maya Chen: yes we support BYOK and HSM, there are two patterns: Redwood-managed envelope keys with customer root, or full customer-hosted keys in your cloud KMS with our key-consumer integration. there are tradeoffs for escrow and rotation we can walk through.
[01:50] Ben Carter: what about log access? procurement wants to know audit log retention for token-level traces and request metadata.
[02:04] Daniel Ruiz: we capture audit logs and can stream to your SIEM, retention is configurable; standard hosted retention is 90 days but for enterprise we can extend or export to S3/Cloud Storage. note, we redact PII by default but you can opt for full payload retention under terms.
[02:30] Laila Gomez: on the MSA the DPA has some language around processor/subprocessor that we need to amend — specifically the subprocessor notification window, 30 days is fine but we need explicit right to object. also liability caps need clarity if data residency is breached.
[02:50] Lina Park: noted, we typically accept a 30-day notice with an objection right, happy to take your redlines and mark them up. our legal is used to standard cloud vendor phrasing but we can capture exceptions. can you share the clause you want changed now?
[03:08] Laila Gomez: it's Section 4.2 subprocessing notice and Section 11 liability. i'll flag them in the doc but want to understand Redwood's approach to escrow or indemnity in practice.
[03:25] Lina Park: okay we'll follow up with the annotated MSA. next on egress/billing — sofia, you said you need granular egress scenarios, any particular traffic shape?
[03:40] Sofia Ruiz: we anticipate heavy embedding traffic for search re-indexing monthly and steady chat/generation at peak hours. need to see cost under both continuous small requests and batch embedding jobs.
[03:55] Daniel Ruiz: got it — typically we separate token compute charges from egress/transfer charges. for hosted customers compute is per-token and egress is network transfer + persisted storage if you pull embeddings out. we can model sample monthly volumes; i'll prepare three scenarios (low/med/high) and show how dedicated capacity changes unit economics.
[04:20] Priya Nair: on dedicated vs hosted we're leaning hosted initially for speed but want predictability; how does dedicated pricing tie into SLOs?
[04:35] Lina Park: dedicated comes with reserved throughput and SLA-backed latency percentiles; hosted is more elastic but has multi-tenant fallback. for mission-critical we recommend dedicated with canary rollouts.
[04:52] Omar Haddad: do you support regional routing—we need EU-only processing for certain assets.
[05:04] Daniel Ruiz: yes we have region pinning; private deployments are also available if you need full control. note there is a deployment setup time for private, usually 4-8 weeks depending on environment.
[05:24] Sofia Ruiz: back to KMS — if we use our KMS, what's the key rotation process and who has access to key material?
[05:38] Maya Chen: if using customer KMS we never see raw key material; we get a key handle and can request decrypt/encrypt ops. rotation is transparent to the app with versioned keys. for HSM-backed setups we can integrate with your HSM provider, but some onboarding work is required.
[05:58] [break in audio for ~7s]
[06:07] Ben Carter: about benchmarks, we want a sample of 100 concurrent inference calls with mean latency under 120 ms — is that feasible?
[06:22] Daniel Ruiz: depends on model and sequence length; for trimmed LLMs and quantized weights that's possible on dedicated pools. for hosted it depends on current load. we should run a pilot with your request profiles.
[06:39] Priya Nair: product question — do you do token-level cost visibility per route? we need to tag requests per team.
[06:52] Jordan Patel: yes, our console provides per-route and token-level breakdowns, you can create route tags and set quotas. we'll show a demo if useful.
[07:06] Sofia Ruiz: procurement also alerts on data residency clauses — do you support contractual commitments on residency?
[07:17] Lina Park: we can contractually commit to regionally processing and specify egress paths; for strict residency we usually recommend private deployment or dedicated in-region pools.
[07:34] Laila Gomez: another legal ask — we require SOC2 Type II evidence and a point of contact for audits.
[07:46] Maya Chen: we can provide our SOC2 summary report and SOC auditor contact, and coordinate security questionnaire responses.
[08:00] Sofia Ruiz: can you also confirm your incident response SLAs and notification windows?
[08:12] Daniel Ruiz: standard incident notifications are 1 hour for Sev 1, with follow-up timelines; for enterprise we can agree to shorter windows and escalation contacts.
[08:28] Omar Haddad: encryption in transit and at rest, key separation — we need to ensure model cache isn't exposing customer tokens.
[08:41] Daniel Ruiz: we isolate KV cache per-customer and encrypt at rest; the runtime keeps kv-cache in memory for speed but we have controls to evict and we can configure TTLs. sometimes transcripts show as partial payload — we'll include data handling appendix.
[08:59] Priya Nair: who is responsible for data breach notifications in the MSA?
[09:10] Lina Park: the MSA sets mutual obligations but generally Redwood commits to notify within 72 hours and support the investigation. we'll take note if you need shorter notice windows.
[09:26] Sofia Ruiz: ok procurement question — do you offer escrow or price protection for pilot -> prod transition?
[09:38] Lina Park: we offer pricing floors and committed usage discounts for dedicated contracts. escrow for source/model code is negotiable in enterprise deals; we can add a clause.
[09:52] Ben Carter: any restrictions on model quantization or third-party weights?
[09:59] Daniel Ruiz: we host curated open models and also allow customer model variants; quantization is supported but validated for quality. if you bring your own weights, we'll do a compatibility pass.
[10:12] [Timestamp jump — mid-discussion notes]
[10:30] Sofia Ruiz: procurement would like a single doc that shows total cost for three scenarios including egress, storage, and optional KMS fees.
[10:43] Lina Park: yes that's in the pricing worksheet action. we'll include dedicated vs hosted delta and an estimated timeline to break-even.
[10:58] Laila Gomez: on indemnity we're debating whether vendor indemnity covers customer claims arising from model outputs — this is tricky.
[11:10] Daniel Ruiz: historically indemnity covers breaches and misuse, not model hallucinations; we can discuss carve-outs but generally vendors push back on output liability.
[11:27] Priya Nair: success criteria for pilot are critical — we want latency under X, accuracy on retrieval-based evals not degrade >2% and clear SLOs for uptime.
[11:40] Lina Park: perfect. we'll capture SLOs: p50/p90/p95 latencies, throughput guarantees for dedicated and an accuracy monitor for eval prompts.
[11:54] Ben Carter: can the pilot emulate our production traffic shape (bursty bursts at 4-6 PM PST)?
[12:06] Daniel Ruiz: yes, we can run load tests with your traces or synthetic shaped traffic; that will inform batching and cache config.
[12:20] Sofia Ruiz: there may be a legal stipulation around subprocessor lists; we need the full list for the DPA.
[12:33] Lina Park: we'll provide the current subprocessor list and a process for 30-day notice on changes.
[12:46] Omar Haddad: encryption key escrow — if we need to terminate, can you purge keys and verify deletion?
[12:57] Maya Chen: yes, we have key revocation and deletion processes and can provide attestation for key destruction if part of contract.
[13:12] Laila Gomez: procurement also asked about export controls and data transfer — do you support data residency + egress audit logs?
[13:24] Jordan Patel: yes, we can provide transfer logs and show egress flows; we'll add that to the security pack.
[13:38] Sofia Ruiz: timeline — our procurement committee meets 2025-01-27; we need Redwood's materials before that.
[13:50] Lina Park: we'll target sending the MSA/DPA annotated draft and pricing before 2025-01-15 to give you time.
[14:04] [mid-call — demo mention] Daniel Ruiz: briefly, the SE demo will show per-route metrics and how egress is accounted in the console — we can schedule a 20m demo for that.
[14:20] Priya Nair: sounds good, but security wants to see the SOC2 and architecture diagram first.
[14:30] Maya Chen: we'll include architecture diagram with region boundaries, KMS flow and log pipeline.
[14:45] Sofia Ruiz: is there an on-prem option? some of our data categories might require airgapped handling.
[14:56] Daniel Ruiz: we do an on-prem package but it's a larger engagement; often customers start hosted then migrate to private. on-prem lead time typically 6-12 weeks.
[15:12] Ben Carter: going back to costs, how do you bill for long-running embedding jobs that consume heavy GPU time?
[15:24] Lina Park: for batch jobs we offer job-based billing or time-based GPU consumption; we'll present both models. you can also pre-stage to reduce egress by storing embeddings in your VPC.
[15:41] Priya Nair: any mandatory SLA credits?
[15:48] Lina Park: standard SLA credits apply for availability breaches; enterprise deals can negotiate different credit terms.
[15:59] Laila Gomez: question: who holds the encryption keys for logs? if we export logs to our S3, who retains control?
[16:10] Maya Chen: if logs are exported to your storage, you control the keys; if we host logs, default is Redwood-managed with options for customer KMS.
[16:25] [short pause]
[16:30] Sofia Ruiz: can you confirm the pilot acceptance criteria in writing? procurement wants a clear go/no-go checklist.
[16:40] Lina Park: yes we'll produce an acceptance checklist: performance thresholds, eval pass rates, security checklist, and legal signoff items.
[16:55] Daniel Ruiz: action: i'll draft a pilot test plan including traffic shape, dataset, and acceptance thresholds.
[17:06] Ben Carter: will the pilot run against our prod-like data or synthetic? we prefer redacted prod traces.
[17:16] Daniel Ruiz: redacted traces are fine; we can provide a scrub script and guidelines.
[17:27] Laila Gomez: about the DPA, we may need a clause for processor audits; can Redwood support onsite or remote audit access?
[17:38] Jordan Patel: we support remote audit evidence and can coordinate with your auditors; onsite audits are evaluated case-by-case.
[17:50] Sofia Ruiz: procurement wants to know termination terms — if we pull out after X months can we export all embeddings and logs?
[18:02] Lina Park: yes data export is included in the exit clause; we can add an extended export window if needed.
[18:15] Priya Nair: okay i think we have enough to move forward, the immediate needs are the annotated MSA/DPA, pricing scenarios and security pack.
[18:27] Lina Park: great. to reiterate next steps we'll send items by mid next week and schedule the benchmark.
[18:36] Sofia Ruiz: procurement will review the pricing spreadsheet and come back with a shortlist of exceptions.
[18:44] Laila Gomez: i'll compile legal exceptions and share by 2025-01-20.
[18:52] Daniel Ruiz: one technical note — when we model egress charges we'll include both egress transfer and any storage retrieval fees from your cloud.
[19:05] Ben Carter: what's the estimate for benchmark runtime? 2-3 hours?
[19:12] Daniel Ruiz: depends on traffic profile but plan for a 2-hour window plus prep.
[19:22] Priya Nair: can we get a price estimate for dedicated 24/7 pool vs a shared hosted tier?
[19:33] Lina Park: yes, that will be in the worksheet — we'll show committed monthly vs on-demand.
[19:45] [closing minutes]
[19:50] Lina Park: ok final quick recap: Redwood will send annotated MSA/DPA, pricing & egress scenarios, security pack (SOC2, architecture, subprocessor list), and SE will schedule a benchmark. customer will review legal exceptions and procurement will circle back.
[20:12] Sofia Ruiz: thanks all, we'll aim to have internal feedback by 1/20.
[20:20] Lina Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links. bye.

Notes on transcript: auto-transcription picked up some overlapping talk and occasional mis-heard acronyms (K V cache transcribed as KV catche), names occasionally as similar-sounding (Aurelius sometimes 'Orilius'), filler words left in.

additional_context: Customer is mid-market fintech, procurement timeline tight with committee on 2025-01-27. Pilot planned for Feb. Primary blockers: DPA redlines, KMS escrow, egress cost modeling. Redwood to provide security pack and pricing scenarios.
